newsitem.title: USA: US Fed's Phillips sees need for global cooperation.
newsitem.headline: US Fed's Phillips sees need for global cooperation.

text.p: Global financial regulators will be forced to cooperate further because of the rapid pace of change and innovation in world markets, Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said in a speech Tuesday.

"Firms in need of international financial services will utilize domestic or foreign financial institutions to the extent their prices are competitive and their financial stability can be assured," Phillips said in a prepared speech for an International Monetary Fund seminar here.
"As a result, regulators are recognizing the need to harmonize laws and regulations," she said.
Harmonization of rules will not necessarily require every country to adopt identical rules, Phillips said.

"That we need some level of conformity seems quite clear," Phillips said. "Otherwise the inconsistency and incompatibility of rules and regulations across countries may make it difficult, if not impossible, for some firms to engage in global business activities."
"I submit that it may be less important that we standardize particular banking laws and regulations, than it is for us to pursue similiar goals," she said.
